title_en: Wuhan Zhonglian Securities Labor Service Company v. Hong Kong-Macau Xiangqing Industry — dispute over return of property
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 85 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, when a people's court tries a civil case and conducts mediation with the voluntary consent of the parties, it must also distinguish right from wrong on the basis of clear facts.
keywords_en: civil; dispute over return of property; retrial; Supreme People's Court; Hubei Province; Macao Special Administrative Region; legal person; Civil Procedure Law; whether the mediation agreement harms the interests of third parties; conditions for initiating retrial; reversal of judgment; cooperative development agreement; equity transfer; enforcement of mediation document; voluntary mediation; distinguishing right from wrong; securities; application for retrial; Hong Kong and Macao Xiangqing Industrial return of property dispute
full_text_en:
Wuhan Zhonglian Securities Labor Service Company v. Hong Kong-Macau Xiangqing Industry — Dispute over Return of Property

Ruling Summary

1. Pursuant to Article 85 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, when a people's court hears a civil case and conducts mediation on a voluntary basis by the parties, it must also distinguish between right and wrong on the basis of clear facts.

2. With respect to a legally effective mediation statement, if the parties have not applied for a retrial, but the legitimate rights and interests of a third party not involved in the case are harmed, and the people's court discovers that there is indeed an error and that a retrial is necessary, the people's court may conduct a retrial in accordance with the trial supervision procedure.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2005) Min Si Ti Zi No. 1

Plaintiff at First Instance: Wuhan Zhonglian Securities Labor Service Company, domiciled at No. 9 Qingdao Road, Jiang'an District, Wuhan, Hubei Province.

Legal Representative: Ding Daochun, Manager of the Company.

Defendant at First Instance: Hong Kong-Macau Xiangqing Industry, domiciled at Shop 1, G/F, Dequn Building, No. 26 Rua do Loreto, Macau Special Administrative Region.

Legal Representative: Zheng Yangguang, Chairman of the Company.

Authorized Agent: Guan Anping, Lawyer of Beijing Anpingcheng Law Firm.

Authorized Agent: Peng Xuejun, Lawyer of Beijing Anpingcheng Law Firm.

With respect to the dispute over return of property between the plaintiff at first instance, Wuhan Zhonglian Securities Labor Service Company (hereinafter referred to as Zhonglian Company), and the defendant at first instance, Hong Kong-Macau Xiangqing Industry (hereinafter referred to as Macau Xiangqing), the Hubei High People's Court rendered a civil mediation statement, (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73, on November 7, 1996, which has become legally effective. Because the party Macau Xiangqing applied for a retrial, the Hubei High People's Court, after retrial, rendered a civil mediation statement, (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 10, on March 23, 2001. Subsequently, because a third party not involved in the case, Macau FuChang Real Estate, raised an objection, the Hubei High People's Court conducted a second retrial of this case and rendered a civil ruling, (2003) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 5, on September 5, 2003. Upon review, this Court rendered a civil ruling, (2005) Min Si Jian Zi No. 19, on July 15, 2005, ordering a trial de novo of this case. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel with trial judge Lu Xiaolong serving as presiding judge, acting trial judges Ren Xuefeng and Gao Xiaoli participating in the deliberation, and Liu Yongshen serving as court clerk, and held a public hearing of this case on November 17, 2005. Zheng Yangguang, the legal representative of Macau Xiangqing, and his authorized agents Guan Anping and Peng Xuejun appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. Zhonglian Company, after being lawfully summoned by this Court, failed to appear in court without justifiable cause. This case is now concluded.

The following facts were found by the Hubei High People's Court at first instance: On November 16, 1994, Macau Xiangqing and Zhonglian Company entered into an agreement for the cooperative development of the air-conditioned waiting hall at Shijiazhuang Railway Station, stipulating that by the end of November 1994, Macau Xiangqing would contribute RMB 11,000,000 and Zhonglian Company would contribute RMB 9,000,000, with the investment to be recovered within 18 months and interest calculated at an annual rate of 25%; after recovery of the investment, the operating income from the Shijiazhuang Railway Station waiting hall project for the remaining 8 years and 6 months would be distributed at 55% to Macau Xiangqing and 45% to Zhonglian Company. After the agreement was signed, Zhonglian Company, as agreed, remitted the investment of RMB 9,000,000 to Macau Xiangqing. On April 5, 1995, Macau Xiangqing, in its own name, entered into a cooperative operation contract with Shijiazhuang Railway Station Huatong General Company to jointly operate the waiting hall at Shijiazhuang Railway Station, with Macau Xiangqing holding a 45% share. On March 23, 1996, Macau Xiangqing issued a "Share Transfer Certificate" to Zhonglian Company, stating: "If my company cannot repay the investment principal and return on investment totaling RMB 12,375,000 owed to Zhonglian Company before June 30, 1996, my company is willing to transfer all of its 45% shares in the Shijiazhuang Railway Station waiting hall project to Zhonglian Company." Because Macau Xiangqing failed to perform its obligations, Zhonglian Company filed a lawsuit against Macau Xiangqing as defendant in the Hubei High People's Court on August 27, 1996, seeking payment of the investment principal of RMB 9,000,000 and the agreed return on investment of RMB 3,375,000, together with overdue interest. During the trial, with the mediation of the Hubei High People's Court, the parties reached the following agreement: 1. Macau Xiangqing shall pay Zhonglian Company the investment principal of RMB 9,000,000, the return on investment of RMB 3,370,000, and overdue interest of RMB 810,000, totaling RMB 13,180,000, before December 31, 1996. In case of late payment, execution shall be carried out in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law. 2. Case acceptance fee of RMB 81,885, other litigation fees of RMB 8,115, and property preservation fee of RMB 62,395, totaling RMB 142,395, shall be borne by Zhonglian Company in the amount of RMB 71,197.50 and by Macau Xiangqing in the amount of RMB 71,197.50. The litigation fees and property preservation fee, totaling RMB 142,395, have been prepaid by Zhonglian Company, and Macau Xiangqing shall pay its share to Zhonglian Company before December 31, 1996. The Hubei High People's Court rendered a civil mediation statement, (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73, on November 7, 1996, confirming the above agreement.

Thereafter, Macau Xiangqing applied to the Hubei High People's Court for a retrial on the grounds that the content of the mediation statement (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 of the Hubei High People's Court was illegal. The Hubei High People's Court rendered a civil ruling, (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zi No. 70, on March 12, 2001, deciding to conduct a retrial of the case (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73.

The Hubei High People's Court confirmed the facts found at first instance during the retrial. During the trial, with the mediation of the Hubei High People's Court, the parties voluntarily reached the following agreement: 1. The agreement on cooperative development of the waiting hall at Shijiazhuang Railway Station entered into by Macau Xiangqing and Zhonglian Company is dissolved, and Wuhan Yinqing Property Co., Ltd. is dissolved; 2. Macau Xiangqing shall return the principal of RMB 9,000,000 to Zhonglian Company and pay corresponding occupation fees and other compensation of RMB 4,740,000; 3. Zhonglian Company shall return to Macau Xiangqing, based on actual circumstances, all income and funds (including the execution funds from the original trial) obtained from Shijiazhuang Jiqing Service Co., Ltd. and its renamed entity Shijiazhuang Jichang Service Co., Ltd. The amount shall be liquidated by Macau Xiangqing and Zhonglian Company within one month after this mediation statement takes effect, and Zhonglian Company does not hold any equity in the aforesaid service companies. 4. After offsetting items 2 and 3 above, any shortfall or excess shall, from the date this agreement takes effect, incur occupation fees calculated by stages based on the one-year floating loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China. After liquidation, any issues arising from changes in equity of the aforesaid service companies shall be handled by Macau Xiangqing. 5. The litigation fees, property preservation fees, and execution fees from the original trial shall be borne by Zhonglian Company (already performed), and the retrial litigation fee of RMB 68,700 shall be borne by Macau Xiangqing. The Hubei High People's Court rendered a civil mediation statement, (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 10, on March 23, 2001, confirming the above agreement. In this mediation statement, the Hubei High People's Court also stated: This mediation statement shall have legal effect upon receipt and signature by both parties, and the civil mediation statement (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 and the civil rulings (1997) E Zhi Zi No. 5-1 and 5-2 of this Court shall be deemed vacated.

Because a third party not involved in the case raised an objection during the execution of the civil mediation statement (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 10, the Hubei High People's Court again rendered a civil ruling, (2002) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zi No. 54, on June 28, 2002, deciding to conduct a retrial of this case. After another retrial, the Hubei High People's Court rendered a civil ruling, (2003) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 5, which found the following: After the civil mediation statement (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 of this Court became legally effective, Macau Xiangqing failed to perform the obligations specified in that mediation statement. During execution, this Court compulsorily transferred Macau Xiangqing's 45% equity in the former Shijiazhuang Jiqing Travel Service Co., Ltd. to Zhonglian Company. On May 26, 1997, Zhonglian Company entered into an agreement with Macau FuChang Real Estate, agreeing to transfer the aforesaid 45% equity in the enterprise to Macau FuChang Real Estate for value. In July of the same year, this Court issued a ruling to sell the aforesaid 45% equity in the enterprise to Macau FuChang Real Estate. It was also found that the aforementioned Macau FuChang Real Estate was established in 1991, registered with the Macau Finance Department under the name of taxpayer Weng Wenxiong, with business tax file number 52286, and had ceased operations in April 1998; Weng Wenxiong died in April 1998. The Macau FuChang Real Estate that raised an objection to this Court was established in April 2001, registered with the Macau Finance Department under the name of taxpayer Weng Dehui, with business tax file number 98349. There is no legal succession of property between this Macau FuChang Real Estate (hereinafter referred to as New FuChang Real Estate) and the aforementioned Macau FuChang Real Estate (hereinafter referred to as Old FuChang Real Estate). The Hubei High People's Court held: Old FuChang Real Estate, which participated in this case during this Court's execution, had a legal interest in this case but ceased operations in April 1998. However, New FuChang Real Estate, which raised an objection to this Court, did not participate in the trial or execution of this case and does not have a legal interest in this case. Its objection filed with this Court in September 2001 was made by falsely using the name of Old FuChang Real Estate, which had a license holder of Weng Wenxiong and had already ceased operations. The factual findings in this Court's civil ruling (2002) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zi No. 54 were erroneous. After discussion by the trial committee of this Court, and in accordance with Article 140, paragraph 1, item (11) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 109 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and with reference to Article 201 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it was ruled as follows: This Court's civil ruling (2002) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zi No. 54 and civil ruling (2003) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 5-1 are vacated.

During the trial de novo before this Court, with respect to the facts found in the civil mediation statement (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 of the Hubei High People's Court, Macau Xiangqing raised no objection to the other facts except for the statement that "Zhonglian Company, as agreed, remitted the investment of RMB 9,000,000 to Macau Xiangqing," which it claimed was a clerical error. As to the facts concerning the remittance, Macau Xiangqing contended that the RMB 9,000,000 was first remitted by Zhonglian Company to Wuhan Yinqing Property Co., Ltd., rather than directly to Macau Xiangqing, but Macau Xiangqing acknowledged its occupation of the funds. Therefore, this Court confirms the facts affirmed in the civil mediation statement (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73, except that the statement that Zhonglian Company, as agreed, remitted the investment of RMB 9,000,000 to Macau Xiangqing is a clerical error; the other facts are supported by relevant evidence and are not disputed by the parties. As to the facts concerning the remittance, this Court finds that Zhonglian Company first remitted RMB 9,000,000 to Wuhan Yinqing Property Co., Ltd., after which the funds were occupied by Macau Xiangqing.

This Court also found the following facts: On November 5, 1996, Zheng Yangguang, the legal representative of Macau Xiangqing, signed on behalf of Macau Xiangqing the mediation agreement in the case (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73. Zhonglian Company received and signed for the civil mediation statement (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 of the Hubei High People's Court on November 11, 1996. Li Guoqiang, on behalf of Macau Xiangqing, received and signed for the mediation statement (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 on November 12, 1996. When Li Guoqiang received and signed for the mediation statement, he submitted to the people's court a power of attorney, which stated: "I hereby appoint Mr. Li Guoqiang, Vice General Manager of the Company, as the fully authorized representative in charge of handling the mediation activities concerning the dispute over the cooperative development project contract brought by Wuhan Zhonglian Securities Labor Service Company against the Company." The power of attorney bore the seal of Macau Xiangqing and was also signed by Chairman Zheng Yangguang.

Because Macau Xiangqing failed to perform the obligations specified in the civil mediation statement (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73, Zhonglian Company applied to the Hubei High People's Court for enforcement. During the enforcement process, the Hubei High People's Court rendered a civil ruling, (1997) E Zhi Zi No. 5-1, on March 4, 1997. The ruling stated that the applicant for enforcement was Zhonglian Company and the person subject to enforcement was Macau Xiangqing. The Hubei High People's Court ruled to withdraw and pay to Zhonglian Company the dividends (as of February 28, 1997) of Macau Xiangqing in Shijiazhuang Jiqing Travel Service Co., Ltd. to satisfy part of the debt; and to transfer Macau Xiangqing's 45% equity in Shijiazhuang Jiqing Travel Service Co., Ltd. to Zhonglian Company from March 1, 1997, to satisfy the debt. Thereafter, Zhonglian Company further applied to have the equity of Macau Xiangqing, which had been transferred to Zhonglian Company by the Hubei High People's Court's ruling, sold to Old FuChang Real Estate. The Hubei High People's Court rendered a civil ruling, (1997) E Zhi Zi No. 5-2, on September 14, 1997, ruling to sell Macau Xiangqing's 45% interest in the former Shijiazhuang Jiqing Travel Service Co., Ltd. to Old FuChang Real Estate to satisfy the debt of the creditor Zhonglian Company. After the above rulings were made, the parties went through the procedures for approval and change of registration, and Old FuChang Real Estate obtained the equity in the cooperative enterprise.

Because Macau Xiangqing was dissatisfied with the civil mediation statement (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 of the Hubei High People's Court, it filed a petition with the Hubei High People's Court on April 5, 2000. The grounds for its petition were: (1) Macau Xiangqing never received or signed for the mediation statement, nor did it authorize or appoint any other person to receive or sign for it. Although the mediation statement was received and signed by Li Guoqiang on the basis of a power of attorney with no clear authorization, Li Guoqiang's receipt and signature constituted an act exceeding his authority and did not have legal effect on Macau Xiangqing; the mediation statement did not take effect, and there was no legal basis for its enforcement. (2) The RMB 9,000,000 that Zhonglian Company requested Macau Xiangqing to repay was an investment made by both parties to jointly establish Wuhan Yinqing Property Co., Ltd. Zhonglian Company's lawsuit for that sum lacked both contractual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

It was also found: For the purpose of enforcing the civil mediation statement (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 10, the Hubei High People's Court rendered a ruling, (2001) E Zhi Zi No. 16-1, on September 21, 2001, ruling to revert to Macau Xiangqing the 45% equity held by Old FuChang Real Estate in Shijiazhuang Jichang Travel Service Co., Ltd. (formerly Shijiazhuang Jiqing Travel Service Co., Ltd.).

New FuChang Real Estate and Weng Dehui, because they had objections to the civil mediation statement (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 10 and the civil ruling (2003) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 5 of the Hubei High People's Court, reported to this Court stating: 1. FuChang Real Estate's equity in Shijiazhuang Jichang Travel Service Co., Ltd. was lawfully acquired. FuChang Real Estate had already paid the equity transfer price, and the equity should be protected by law. FuChang Real Estate's acquisition of the equity had no legal causal relationship with the dispute over return of property between Macau Xiangqing and Zhonglian Company. 2. When conducting the retrial in 2001, the Hubei High People's Court directly rendered the mediation statement (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 10 involving the disposition of equity under the name of FuChang Real Estate without notifying FuChang Real Estate, thereby disposing of the lawful rights and interests of others. This was illegal in content and should be vacated. Moreover, Macau Xiangqing's application for retrial had already exceeded the two-year statute of limitations. 3. In issuing the corresponding ruling for reversal of enforcement during execution, the Hubei High People's Court had executed the property of a third party not involved in the case, seriously infringing upon the civil rights and procedural rights of FuChang Real Estate. 4. Although New FuChang Real Estate and Old FuChang Real Estate were separately registered with the Macau Finance Department, New FuChang Real Estate had in fact succeeded to all the rights and obligations of Old FuChang Real Estate and was entitled to succeed to the foreign equity in the aforesaid cooperative enterprise. Alternatively, Weng Dehui, as the lawful heir of Weng Wenxiong, was fully entitled, as an heir, to claim the equity of Old FuChang Real Estate. The civil ruling (2003) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 5 of the Hubei High People's Court, which dismissed the objection of New FuChang Real Estate and ignored the objection raised by Weng Dehui in his capacity as an heir, lacked legal basis.

This Court, upon trial, holds: After the Hubei High People's Court rendered the civil mediation statement (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 at first instance, during the enforcement process, Old FuChang Real Estate lawfully obtained the equity of the former Macau Xiangqing in the mainland cooperative enterprise, and went through the relevant approval and change of registration procedures, becoming a shareholder of the cooperative enterprise. Weng Wenxiong, the license holder of Old FuChang Real Estate, died in 1998, and Old FuChang Real Estate had ceased operations in April 1998. New FuChang Real Estate was established in April 2001, with Weng Dehui as the license holder. New FuChang Real Estate failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove that it succeeded to the rights and obligations of Old FuChang Real Estate in law; therefore, it cannot be determined that New FuChang Real Estate has a legal interest in this case. Old FuChang Real Estate participated in this case due to the enforcement of the mediation statement (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73. The result of the retrial of this case, particularly the enforcement measures taken, has a legal interest for Old FuChang Real Estate. Old FuChang Real Estate has ceased operations, and its license holder Weng Wenxiong has died. Based on the declaration of Yu Caichan, the wife of Weng Wenxiong (mother of Weng Dehui), relevant identity documents, and the minutes of the estate administrator's statement before the Macau Primary Court, it can be determined that Weng Dehui, the daughter of Weng Wenxiong, is the lawful heir of Weng Wenxiong, and she has accepted the entrustment of other heirs to temporarily manage the relevant property. Therefore, Weng Dehui is a third party not involved in the case that has an interest in this case and is entitled to report the relevant circumstances to the people's court concerning the relevant rights and interests of Old FuChang Real Estate. Moreover, even if a third party not involved in the case has no interest in the case, based on the circumstances it reports, if a higher people's court discovers that a legal document issued by a lower people's court indeed contains an error and still needs to be corrected, it shall be corrected. Pursuant to this Court's Reply No. (93) Min Ta Zi No. 1 on the Issue of Whether a People's Court May Retry a Case Where a Mediation Statement Indeed Contains an Error but the Parties Have Not Applied for Retrial, with respect to a legally effective mediation statement, if the people's court discovers that there is indeed an error and that a retrial is necessary, even if the parties have not applied for retrial, the people's court may conduct a retrial in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law and the trial supervision procedure.

Article 204 of this Court's "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China" provides: Where a party applies for retrial of a legally effective mediation agreement, the provisions of Article 182 of the Civil Procedure Law shall apply, and the application shall be filed within two years after the mediation agreement becomes legally effective. The two parties to the (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 civil mediation agreement signed and received the mediation agreement on November 11 and 12, 1996, respectively, and the effective date of the mediation agreement was November 12, 1996. Macau Xiangqing did not file an application for retrial within the two-year period prescribed by law. The case file shows that it only filed a complaint with the Hubei High People's Court on April 5, 2000. The grounds for Macau Xiangqing's complaint were: (1) Macau Xiangqing never signed for receipt of the mediation agreement, nor did it entrust or designate any other person to sign for receipt of the mediation agreement. Although the mediation agreement was signed for receipt by Li Guoqiang based on a power of attorney that did not specify clear authorized matters, his signing for receipt constituted unauthorized agency and did not have legal effect on Macau Xiangqing; the mediation agreement did not take effect, and there is no legal basis for enforcement in this case. (2) The 9,000,000 yuan that Zhonglian Company requested Macau Xiangqing to repay constituted an investment in Wuhan Yinqing Property Co., Ltd., a joint venture established by both parties. Zhonglian Company's lawsuit for this amount lacked contractual and legal basis and should be dismissed. According to the facts found, in this case, Zheng Yanguang, as the chairman of the board and legal representative of Macau Xiangqing, signed the mediation agreement in Case No. (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 on behalf of the company on November 5, 1996. Thereafter, Zheng Yanguang, in his capacity as chairman, issued a power of attorney on November 7, 1996, which stated: "I hereby entrust Mr. Li Guoqiang, Deputy General Manager of our company, as the fully authorized representative to be responsible for handling the mediation activities concerning the cooperative development engineering contract dispute between Wuhan Zhonglian Securities Labor Service Company and our company." The power of attorney was affixed with the seal of Macau Xiangqing and also bore the signature of Chairman Zheng Yanguang. The content of this power of attorney sufficiently indicated that Li Guoqiang had the authority to sign for receipt of the mediation agreement on behalf of Macau Xiangqing. The (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 mediation agreement was signed and received by both parties and became effective; Macau Xiangqing's first ground for complaint cannot be established. The cooperative development project of the Shijiazhuang Railway Station waiting hall between Macau Xiangqing and Zhonglian Company was not actually carried out. Macau Xiangqing entered into another cooperative operation contract with a third party for the joint operation of the Shijiazhuang Railway Station waiting hall and occupied Zhonglian Company's 9,000,000 yuan funds. Based on the cooperative development agreement, Zhonglian Company filed a lawsuit with the People's Court against Macau Xiangqing as the defendant, requesting the return of the funds, rather than requesting Wuhan Yinqing Property Co., Ltd. to return the investment. Macau Xiangqing and Zhonglian Company voluntarily reached a mediation agreement, in which Macau Xiangqing promised to return the relevant funds it occupied. The People's Court issued a mediation agreement to confirm this, which complies with legal provisions. Macau Xiangqing's second ground for complaint also cannot be established. The Hubei High People's Court decided to retry the (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 civil mediation agreement. However, neither the ruling deciding the retrial nor the (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 10 civil mediation agreement made after the retrial explained the reasons for deciding the retrial or how the (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 mediation agreement was illegal. The retrial lacked factual and legal basis.

The (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 10 civil mediation agreement made by the Hubei High People's Court after retrying the (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 civil mediation agreement, in addition to maintaining all the contents of the original mediation agreement, added a clause requiring Zhonglian Company to return to Macau Xiangqing all proceeds and funds (including the original trial enforcement payment) obtained from Shijiazhuang Jichang Service Co., Ltd. (formerly Shijiazhuang Jiqing Service Co., Ltd.), and that Zhonglian Company shall not have any equity in the cooperative enterprise. The enforcement payment referred to in this clause is the amount Zhonglian Company obtained by enforcing the (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 mediation agreement. The (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 10 civil mediation agreement, while maintaining the contents of the (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 civil mediation agreement, also confirmed that Zhonglian Company should return the original enforcement payment to Macau Xiangqing. The contents are contradictory and fail to distinguish right from wrong, violating the provisions of Article 85 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which stipulates that when trying civil cases, the People's Courts shall conduct mediation on a voluntary basis by the parties, distinguishing right from wrong based on clear facts. In this case, Zhonglian Company, as the plaintiff, filed a lawsuit requesting the defendant Macau Xiangqing to bear liability. Neither at the first instance nor at the retrial did Macau Xiangqing file a counterclaim. However, the (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 10 civil mediation agreement made by the Hubei High People's Court after retrial confirmed the content of Zhonglian Company, the plaintiff, returning funds to the defendant Macau Xiangqing. There are procedural problems, violating the basic principle of civil litigation that "no trial without complaint." Even if there were problems in enforcement, they should be resolved through enforcement procedures and should not be used as grounds for applying for retrial to be resolved through trial supervision procedures. Article 89, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China clearly stipulates: "Where an agreement is reached through mediation, the People's Court shall prepare a mediation agreement. The mediation agreement shall state the litigation claims, the facts of the case, and the mediation result." According to this provision, the mediation agreement is a legal document that resolves substantive disputes between the parties. Article 1 of this Court's Fa Shi [1998] No. 17 "Reply on How the People's Court Should Handle Cases Where It Finds That Its Own Order for Pre-Litigation Preservation or Order Made in Enforcement Proceedings Is Indeed Erroneous and Where the People's Procuratorate Challenges Such an Order for Pre-Litigation Preservation" also clearly stipulates: "Where the president of a People's Court finds that an order for pre-litigation preservation or an order made in enforcement proceedings that has already taken legal effect is indeed erroneous and deems it necessary to revoke it, the president shall submit it to the Adjudication Committee for discussion and decision, and then rule to revoke the original order." Therefore, whether an order made by the People's Court in enforcement proceedings should be revoked should not be expressed in a mediation agreement. In the (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 10 civil mediation agreement, the Hubei High People's Court stated that the (1997) E Zhi Zi No. 5-1 and 5-2 civil enforcement orders made by that court for the enforcement of the (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 mediation agreement were deemed revoked, which violates legal provisions. Lao Fuchang Real Estate, based on the (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 civil mediation agreement and relevant enforcement orders, legally acquired the equity of the former Macau Xiangqing in the cooperative enterprise in the mainland. The Hubei High People's Court, without stating any reasons, expressed in the (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 10 mediation agreement that the original enforcement orders were deemed revoked, thereby negating the legal basis for Lao Fuchang Real Estate to acquire the equity and harming the legitimate rights and interests of Lao Fuchang Real Estate.

In summary, the (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 civil mediation agreement of the Hubei High People's Court does not have any illegal circumstances, and Macau Xiangqing's grounds for complaint cannot be established. The Hubei High People's Court decided to retry the case without identifying what error existed in the (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 mediation agreement. The retrial of this case lacks factual and legal basis. Furthermore, the (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 10 civil mediation agreement made after the retrial, while substantively confirming the content previously confirmed in the (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 civil mediation agreement, also confirmed the content of Zhonglian Company, the plaintiff, returning to Macau Xiangqing the enforcement payment obtained from enforcing the (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 civil mediation agreement, without Macau Xiangqing, the defendant, having filed a counterclaim. This violates the provision of Article 85 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China that mediation should be conducted on the basis of distinguishing right from wrong, and also violates the basic principle of "no trial without complaint" in civil litigation. At the same time, the Hubei High People's Court explicitly stated in the mediation agreement that the orders made by that court during the enforcement of the (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 civil mediation agreement were deemed revoked. This violates legal provisions and exceeds the scope of application of a mediation agreement. Although the Hubei High People's Court issued the (2002) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zi No. 54 civil ruling to retry the (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 10 case, it did not address the substantive issues of the case after the retrial. Instead, it issued the (2003) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 5 civil ruling revoking the (2002) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zi No. 54 civil ruling, which involves procedural problems. Pursuant to Articles 85, 177, and 184 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby rules as follows:

1. Revoke the (2003) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 5 civil ruling and the (2001) E Gao Fa Jian Er Min Zai Zi No. 10 civil mediation agreement of the Hubei High People's Court;

2. Uphold the legal validity of the (1996) E Jing Chu Zi No. 73 civil mediation agreement of the Hubei High People's Court.

This judgment is final.
